messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'eu-gpu-pool-3' OOM/autoscale limit hit. queue_length=18230, throttled_requests=4140, 5xx_rate=18%. Trigger: autoscaler reached max_replicas=24 and can't scale further. Related deploy: model-service/v8 rollout (started by deploy-bot ~10m ago).
jen: Paging SRE oncall — I'm on it. Creating incident channel and grabbing initial state.
sam: ML infra here — v8 rollout included new kv-cache indexing change + default_context=122k. We saw median context increase ~3x.
alex: Runtime eng — seeing many long requests holding KV caches and blocking batching. Logs show repeated partial evictions: `kvcache.evictions.rate=0.42` and `batcher.wait_ms p50=110`.
maya: Support — customers reporting increased latency and intermittent 503s, a couple of enterprise tenants got timeouts and opened tickets. Need ETA for mitigation.
jen: Quick action plan: 1) pause rollout, 2) reduce ingress to critical customers only, 3) increase pool if possible, 4) decide rollback. Who can pause the rollout now? @deploy-bot
deploy-bot: Received pause request. Running: `deployctl rollout pause model-service/v8 --by=jen`. Paused at 1965432128.
sam: Thanks. Pausing will prevent new v8 pods from starting, but existing v8 pods still warm up large kv entries. We should step down batch size for v8 routes and enable aggressive kv eviction.
alex: I'm going to flip runtime flag to limit max_context_size per request for v8 routes to 32k. Command: ``curl -X POST https://internal-api.runtime/config -d '{"route":"/v8/*","max_context":32768}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer **'``
jen: Do it and post the response. Also set route-level throttles to protect infra: `rate_limit=50r/s` per tenant for now.
alex: Applied max_context=32768 for v8. API responded 200. Throttles set to 50r/s for non-enterprise tenants.
jen: Observability: can someone pull the queue distribution & autoscaler metrics? I want last 30m.
sam: Pasting trimmed metrics: `gpu_pool.queue.length: [30m avg=9.2k, p95=18.1k]`, `autoscaler.replicas: current=24, target=24, max=24`, `kvcache.size_bytes: +3.7x vs baseline`, `inflight_tokens: p50=12, p95=47`
maya: Customer-impact note: two paying customers A and B affected with 30-45s tail latency and retry storms. Tickets escalated.
jen: Can we spin extra capacity manually? Which cloud limit are we hitting?
sam: We're hitting per-region GPU quota. Provider reports quota exhausted for instance-type A100-80GB in eu-west-1. We can request quota bump but that'll take hours. Short term: move non-critical traffic to smaller quantized model variant (v8-q4) on mixed hardware. Alex can we failover safe-routes to v8-q4?
alex: I can add routing fallback: `route-policy add fallback model-service/v8 -> model-service/v8-q4 when pool_util>0.85`. Applying now.
jen: Apply and confirm traffic shift percentages. We want minimal customer-visible regressions.
alex: Policy in place. Traffic shift starting: 10% -> 40% in 5m steps. Initiated at 1965432240.
reed: Product here — prioritizing enterprise SLAs. For customers A/B we should whitelist and keep them on dedicated pools. Can we pin them to older model v7?
sam: Yes, we can force route pin: `model-router pin tenant/A model-service/v7`. Doing it now.
jen: Good. That should stop their errors. Next: rollback plan if we still see autoscale pressure after fallback. Sam, can you prepare an emergency rollback to v7? How long to full rollback?
sam: Rollback script ready: `deployctl rollout undo model-service/v8 --to=tag:v7 --grace=30s`. Estimated completion 6-8 minutes (draining, warmup).
maya: I'll update the affected tickets: telling customers we paused rollout and are migrating impacted tenants to stable v7; estimated mitigation within 15-25 minutes.
jen: Monitoring now — queue length dropping?
sam: Queue length down to 8.3k (from 18.2k) after throttles + fallback. 5xx rate down to 6%. But autoscaler still capped at 24. dB shows reduced inflight.
jen: Good trend. Next: reduce memory pressure on existing v8 pods. Any runtime knobs for kv-cache eviction aggressive mode?
alex: Enabling `kvcache.eviction_policy=aggressive` for v8 pods. Command: `runtimectl set model-service/v8 --kvcache=evict_aggressive`. Applied at 1965432380.
sam: After eviction change, kvcache.size_bytes started dropping ~25% over 3m. Batch latency p50 down to 70ms.
jen: Ok. Let's wait 10m and see if autoscaler recovers or stays flat. If it doesn't, we roll back.
deploy-bot: Note: paused rollout remains. Current active v8 replicas=6 of 24 (mostly warmups).
jen: Sam, if quota request takes >2h, we schedule rollback. If we need a hotfix for v8 to reduce default_context, can ML team ship a config change that defaults to 16k for v8?
sam: We can push a config override, yes. But rolling that out will also create churn. Prefer to rollback first; then iterate on v8 config offline.
reed: Agreed. Product decision: rollback if any sustained >10% 5xx or >10k queue for next 15m.
maya: Customer comms updated: "We paused the v8 rollout and migrated affected customers to stable model v7. Engineers are mitigating increased latency and retries. We'll update in 15 minutes."
jen: 10m check-in: queue=4.6k, 5xx=3.2%, throttled=1.1k. Trend improving. Will keep channel open.
sam: Preparations for rollback still hot if needed. Standby runbook: `runbook/rollback-v8.md` (internal link).
jen: Final decision at +35m: we will not rollback automatically unless metrics worsen. Keep the pause; ML to submit v8 config change and small test rollout after.
reed: We'll schedule postmortem and impact assessment. Maya, collect list of affected customers and SLA hits.
maya: Collected — customers A/B/C with minor SLA violations, I have opens for refunds/escalations.
jen: Thanks all — I'll close the incident channel when metrics stable for 1 hour. For now, priority is observing and preventing any new v8 pods.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=SEV2 -> mitigated (active mitigations: rollout_paused, route_fallback, throttle_limits, kv_eviction). timestamp=1965432745
jen: :thumbsup: Good work. Postmortem owners: sam (technical root cause & fix), reed (product impact & customers), jen (ops timeline).
